bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to economic security; establishing a prenatal and newborn benefit program to provide financial support to families with newborns; authorizing rulemaking; appropriating money; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 268B.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[268B.40] PRENATAL AND NEWBORN BENEFITS.

Subdivision 1.

Definitions.

(a) For the purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.

(b) "Commissioner" means the commissioner of employment and economic development.

(c) "Health care provider" means:

(1) an individual who is licensed, certified, or otherwise authorized under law to practice in Minnesota in the individual's scope of practice as a:

(i) physician;

(ii) physician assistant;

(iii) osteopath;

(iv) advanced practice registered nurse;

(v) certified professional midwife; or

(vi) birth doula; or

(2) any other individual determined by the commissioner to be capable of providing the documentation required.

(d) "Newborn" means a child no more than six months of age.

Subd. 2.

Establishment.

The commissioner must create a program to provide both prenatal financial support and monthly payments to families with newborns.

Subd. 3.

General eligibility.

(a) To be eligible for program benefits, the applicant must be:

(1) a Minnesota resident; and

(2) applying for benefits based on their legal relationship to a newborn who was born on or after January 1, 2028.

(b) Eligibility for benefits under this program is not subject to any income or asset test.

(c) Eligibility for benefits under this program is not conditioned on employment status.

Subd. 4.

Prenatal financial support.

(a) An applicant may apply for a onetime prenatal benefit of $1,500 no earlier than 90 days before the child's estimated or actual:

(1) due date;

(2) date of adoption; or

(3) date of placement with a legal guardian.

(b) An application for prenatal financial support must be supported by documentation of:

(1) the child's actual or pending birth; and

(2) the applicant's actual or pending legal relationship to the child as the child's biological parent, adoptive parent, or legal guardian.

(c) Documentation in support of an application for prenatal financial support may be provided by:

(1) a health care provider;

(2) an adoption or foster care agency involved in the placement; or

(3) another individual or entity approved by the commissioner.

(d) More than one parent or guardian may be listed on an application, but only one prenatal benefit payment may be issued per child.

Subd. 5.

Newborn financial support.

(a) An applicant may apply for a newborn financial support benefit of $750 a month for 24 consecutive months no earlier than the child's:

(1) date of birth;

(2) date of adoption; or

(3) date of placement with a legal guardian.

(b) An application for newborn financial support must be supported by documentation of:

(1) the child's birth; and

(2) the applicant's legal relation to the newborn as the child's biological parent, adoptive parent, or legal guardian.

(c) Documentation in support of an application for newborn financial support may be provided in the form of:

(1) a birth certificate;

(2) a verification of birth form and corresponding vital records;

(3) a legal record of the adoption; or

(4) official documentation of the foster placement.

(d) More than one parent or guardian may be listed on an application, but only one monthly newborn benefit payment may be issued per newborn.

(e) An applicant is ineligible for the benefit under this subdivision for any month where the applicant and newborn are not residents of Minnesota.

Subd. 6.

Application process.

An applicant must apply for prenatal and newborn benefits using a process developed by the commissioner. This process must allow an applicant the option to apply online, by mail, or in person.

Subd. 7.

Change in status.

An applicant must notify the commissioner in writing of any change in the applicant's status as a parent or legal guardian while an application is pending or while the applicant is receiving benefits.

Subd. 8.

Cost of living adjustment.

Beginning on July 1, 2030, and by July 1 of every even-numbered year, the commissioner must review and apply an annual cost-of-living adjustment to the amount of both prenatal and newborn benefit payments.

Subd. 9.

Effect on other benefits.

(a) Notwithstanding any law to the contrary, cash payments under this section must not be considered income, assets, or personal property for purposes of determining eligibility or recertifying eligibility for:

(1) child care assistance programs under chapter 142E;

(2) food support under chapter 142F;

(3) the Minnesota family investment program and diversionary work program under chapter 142G;

(4) general assistance and Minnesota supplemental aid under chapter 256D;

(5) housing support under chapter 256I; and

(6) economic assistance programs under chapter 256P.

(b) The commissioner must not consider cash payments under this section as income or assets for medical assistance under section 256B.056, subdivision 1a, paragraph (a); 3; or 3c.

Subd. 10.

Rulemaking.

The commissioner may adopt rules for the administration of this section.

Subd. 11.

Outreach.

The commissioner must conduct public outreach in partnership with health care providers, local public health agencies, community-based organizations, and Tribal governments to inform families of the availability of benefits under this program.

Subd. 12.

Evaluation and reporting.

(a) Beginning on February 1, 2029, the commissioner must report to the legislature by February 1 of each odd-numbered year on program participation, expenditures, and outcomes, including any recommendations for changes to benefit levels, duration, or administration.

(b) The commissioner may contract with an independent research organization or academic institution to evaluate program impacts on the well-being of children and families.

EFFECTIVE DATE.

This section is effective January 1, 2028.

Sec. 2. PRENATAL AND NEWBORN BENEFITS; APPROPRIATION.

(a) $....... in fiscal year 2027 is appropriated from the general fund to the commissioner of employment and economic development for prenatal and newborn benefits under Minnesota Statutes, section 268B.40. Of this amount:

(1) up to $....... may be used for program administration;

(2) up to $....... may be used for program outreach; and

(3) up to $....... may be used for program evaluation and reporting.

(b) This appropriation is available until June 30, 2029.
